description: The value is a BodySite object, not a bare CURIE: site is required and is an Uberon term (a descendant of UBERON:0001062, anatomic site); qualifier is an optional list of strings for laterality or position (for example right, left, bilateral). Use this slot only when the Condition could occur in multiple locations and the site is not otherwise implied by the concept; an instance of lung cancer does not need site lung. Production currently writes free text (for example Right arm), which does not conform to BodySite.
Example source variable description: PAD diagnosis: 3=Arterial embolism and/or thrombosis of the lower extremities

description: Use this slot to specify the age of the Participant when the Condition ended. Only use this slot if the Participant had the Condition at one time, but no longer. Target is an integer number of days (BDC-HM unit d). If the source gives years, multiply by 365 (the convention HV production uses) and round to an integer; mark such values as derived. Do not emit years.
Example source variable description: AGE WHEN ASTHMA STOPPED|Asthma: If you no longer have asthma at what age did it stop

description: Use this slot to specify the age of the Participant when the Condition started or was first diagnosed. Only use this if the age at Condition start is different from the age of the Participant at the time of the Condition report. Often this will take the form of a separate variable where the Participant is asked how old they were when the Condition started. If the Participant has never had the Condition, this slot should be empty. Target is an integer number of days (BDC-HM unit d). If the source gives years, multiply by 365 (the convention HV production uses) and round to an integer; mark such values as derived. Do not emit years. A source that gives days from enrollment to the diagnosis (for example Days enrollment to F33 Pulmonary Embolism) is an offset, not an age: age at start = age at enrollment (in days) + offset days, derived from several variables.
Example source variable description: Q4d1. Stroke or cerebrovascular age at diagnosis [Neurological History Form. NHX]|AGE WHEN ASTHMA STARTED|AGE WHEN EMPHYSEMA STARTED|AGE WHEN CHRONIC BRONCHITIS STARTED|Asthma: At about what age did asthma start|Q9b. Age first told you had chronic lung disease? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]|Age first told had diabetes|Days enrollment to F33 Pulmonary Embolism|Days enrollment to PAD

description: This is the slot used to anchor the Condition instance in time: the Participant's age when the Condition was reported, not necessarily when it was first recorded. This value is the same as age at visit, age at adjudication, or age at review. The slot was created for Condition instances that are not associated with a Visit (such as those from adjudication). Target is an integer number of days (BDC-HM unit d). If the source gives years, multiply by 365 (the convention HV production uses) and round to an integer; mark such values as derived. Do not emit years.
Example source variable description: Age at visit 1 [Cohort Visit Derived Variables. Visit 1]

description: Use this slot to link the entity that supports the Condition (a Procedure, MeasurementObservation, Assay, File or QuestionnaireResponse) to the Condition. condition_provenance says who or what asserted the Condition; associated_evidence says what supports it, so the two are separate: having evidence does not by itself make the provenance STUDY_RECORD. Use STUDY_RECORD when the study derived the Condition from that record (an ECG finding, ABI, imaging, BMI); keep PHYSICIAN_ADJUDICATION, DEATH_RECORD or HEALTH_RECORD when those sources asserted the Condition and the evidence merely supports it. Link a record when the variable description or study documentation names it. Sometimes a study record is mentioned but the data are not provided; then link a generic instance. Generic forms, questionnaires and medical history are not evidence, but a specific, published instrument such as the Rose Questionnaire is, as a QuestionnaireResponse. This information might be in the data set description or study documentation and not in the variable description.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation flag [ECG data. Visit 4]|ECG LEFT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY|Peripheral artery disease, version 3 (definition 2), Ankle Brachial Index less than 0.9 for both genders [Ankle Brachial BP Index. ABI34. Visit 3]|ANGINA BY ROSE QUESTIONNAIRE|Obesity - BMI greater than or equal to 30

description: (Required.) This is the slot that links the Condition instance to a Participant. This Participant identifier is often in the same table as the Condition variable.
Example source variable description: De-identified ARIC subject ID|SHARE ID NUMBER|WHI dbGaP Subject ID

description: This is the slot that links the Condition instance to a specific visit, where applicable. This is not required. These are usually described as a Visit or an Exam and they are numbered in chronological order. This information can be contained in the variable description or in a separate variable.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation  [Atrial Fibrillation. ATRFIB21. Visit 2]|Self-Report Atrial Fibrillation by the End of V7 [Cohort Status Derived Variables. STATUS71. Visit 7]|Exam number|VISIT

description: (Required.) A CURIE from Mondo or HPO (preferably Mondo), with the documented OMOP exceptions listed in the Condition Concepts table: Carotid plaque (OMOP:4102124, in ConditionConceptEnum) and Interstitial lung abnormality (OMOP:37472817, not yet in ConditionConceptEnum; BDC-HM issue #277 is open, so do not promote output that uses it before #277 merges; the code's label and validity are not independently verified (Athena 403, Atlas-demo 404), so a human with Athena access must confirm it before any use). Choose the most specific concept the source supports; parents roll up. See the Condition Concepts table for how to assign the CURIE. History-of and family-history variants use the base concept's code, with condition_status and relationship_to_participant carrying the difference (see the next row).

History-of and family-history variants (V1 History of cardiovascular disease, History of heart disease, History of heart failure, History of myocardial infarction, Family history of stroke) use the same concept code as the base condition (Cardiovascular disease, Heart disease, Heart failure, Myocardial infarction, Stroke); do not look for a separate history code. History of X: the base concept with condition_status PRESENT or HISTORICAL as the source supports (see condition_status). Family history: the base concept with relationship_to_participant set to the relative (see relationship_to_participant). V1 History of coronary angioplasty is a Procedure, not a Condition; it belongs in the Procedure guide.
Example source variable description: F136 History of valvular heart disease|HISTORY OF OTHER HEART DISEASE INDICATOR|History of hospitalized HF (from HFAA7B)

description: (Required.) Use this slot to capture who or what asserted the Condition instance. The value must be one of ProvenanceEnum. This information can be found in the source variable description, in the data set description, or in another variable. Test-derived findings (left ventricular hypertrophy, impaired fasting or glucose tolerance, carotid plaque, interstitial lung abnormality, claudication or PAD by criteria, obesity derived from BMI) use STUDY_RECORD with the test as associated_evidence; examination findings (a murmur, wheezing) use WORKING_DIAGNOSIS. Do not pool lab- or algorithm-derived and self-reported Conditions silently.

Use this value when the Condition instance results from a Participant informing the investigators of their own condition status without saying that a doctor diagnosed it (for example a bare Have you ever had X? item). This information often comes from a medical history form or questionnaire.
Example source variable description: Self-Report Atrial Fibrillation by the End of V7 [Cohort Status Derived Variables. STATUS71. Visit 7]|HAS/HAD VALVULAR HEART DISEASE?|EMPHYSEMA: SELF-REPORT|Cardiovascular disease ever|[Medical care]. Heart attack? Q8i [Personal History Form, PHXA04. Visit 3]|Self-reported asthma ever|Asthma: Have you ever had asthma

description: BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded based on a patient self-report that was confirmed by a doctor. Use this value when the Participant reports the Condition and the item itself says a doctor or other health professional diagnosed or confirmed it (for example Has a doctor ever said you have X?, diagnosed by a doctor, CONFIRMED BY A DOCTOR). A bare ever-had item with no doctor mentioned is PATIENT_SELF_REPORT. The Participant is still the reporter; a doctor record that the study itself reviewed is HEALTH_RECORD or PHYSICIAN_ADJUDICATION.
Example source variable description: [Medical history]. Have you ever been told by a physician that you had a stroke, slight stroke, transient ischemic attack or transient ischemic attack [TIA]? Q1 [TIA/Stroke. TIAB03. Visit 1]|Emphysema diagnosed by a health professional reported|Doctor diagnosed asthma|Asthma: Diagnosed by doctor or other health professional|WAS ASTHMA CONFIRMED BY A DOCTOR|Has a doctor said that you have a blood clot in a leg or deep vein thrombosis?

description: BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded following adjudication by one or more physicians. Use this value when the Condition instance results from a physician adjudication: a group of third-party clinical experts reviews Participant data and makes a determination about Condition status, usually by applying case-definition criteria. This is very different from an event review. The information indicating that the Condition was the result of a physician adjudication might be in the data set description rather than in the variable description.
Example source variable description: ENDPT - ASTHMA|PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE ENDPNT

description: Use this value when the Condition instance results from information gathered from a third party (an informant), often because the Participant cannot speak for themselves. INFORMANT_INTERVIEW is valid on BDC-HM main (PR 275) but is not in the 2026-09-06 pinned schema snapshot.
Example source variable description: A. History. EVER HAD STROKE Q18 [Informant Interview Form, IFI]

description: BDC-HM meaning: the Condition was recorded in a death record, a general category that includes death certificates, autopsy records and medical examiner reports. Use this value when the Condition instance results from any of these. DEATH_CERTIFICATE also exists in ProvenanceEnum but this guide does not use it; use DEATH_RECORD.
Example source variable description: OTHER HEART DISEASE? Q6E [Coroner /Medical Examiner Form]|MI IN LAST FOUR WEEKS Q15B [Coroner /Medical Examiner Form]

description: BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded in a study-related record. Use this value when the Condition instance results from data the study collected or derived, for example a MeasurementObservation or a Procedure (an ECG, imaging, BMI). We may or may not be able to link the actual study record in associated_evidence. A hospital record that the study abstracted is HEALTH_RECORD, not STUDY_RECORD.
Example source variable description: Atrial fibrillation flag [ECG data. Visit 4]|Myocardial infarction, by Minnesota code [ECG data. Visit 2]

description: BDC-HM meaning: a review of clinical event information that describes a suspected clinical occurrence without applying standardized case-definition criteria or independent physician review. It does not reflect a validated determination of whether the event meets a formal clinical definition. Use this value when the Condition instance results from such an investigator review of event information. A review that applies case-definition criteria through independent physicians is PHYSICIAN_ADJUDICATION; study-derived data without review is STUDY_RECORD. The information that indicates an event review could be in the data set description rather than in the variable description. EVENT_REVIEW is valid on BDC-HM main (PR 275) but is not in the 2026-09-06 pinned schema snapshot.

BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded in a patient health record. Use this value when the Condition instance results from a hospitalization, discharge or medical-record abstraction (hospital record abstraction forms, discharge summary diagnoses). HOSPITAL_RECORD is not a BDC-HM value; HV production uses HEALTH_RECORD for these records. EHR_DISCHARGE_SUMMARY and EHR_DISCHARGE_RECORD also exist but HEALTH_RECORD is the production convention.
Example source variable description: PE BASED ON HOSP DISCHARGE SUMMARY DIAGNOSIS|PAD based on: Amputation of one or more toes or part of the lower extremity because of ischemia or gangrene|Section 3: Medical History. Respiratory. Asthma [Heart Failure Hospital Record Abstraction Form, HFA]|Angina based on: 70% or greater obstruction of any coronary artery on angiography on this admission

description: BDC-HM value CASE_REPORT_FORM: use when the Condition instance results from a study case report form completed by study staff (not a hospital record and not a participant questionnaire). HV production uses it in some blocks; confirm the form type from the data set description.

BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded as a working diagnosis. Use this value when the Condition instance results from a clinical diagnostic impression or an examination finding (a murmur, wheezing). CLINICAL_DIAGNOSIS is not a ProvenanceEnum value; production blocks that use it should be corrected to WORKING_DIAGNOSIS.
Example source variable description: CLINICAL DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION: OTHER HEART DISEASE: MITRAL VALVE DISEASE|CDI-OTHER PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE

description: BDC-HM meaning: the condition was recorded based on a patient-provided medication report. Use this value when the Condition instance is inferred from a Participant taking medication for the Condition.
Example source variable description: COPD Med Use - self/scanned (ever COPD by MD diag)

description: Use this slot to capture the severity of the Condition, if available (a subjective clinical assessment). Mapping: slight, mild or grade 1 is MILD; moderate or grade 2 is MODERATE; marked, severe or grade 3 is SEVERE. When a more specific concept exists (Morbid obesity, Aortic valve stenosis) use that concept instead of, or in addition to, a severity value; a severity grade does not replace the concept.
Example source variable description: BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY|F136 TTE LVH

description: BDC-HM meaning: a condition that causes minimal symptoms or functional impairment and typically does not require intensive intervention.
Example source variable description: BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 1=SLIGHT|F136 TTE LVH: Mild

description: BDC-HM meaning: a condition that causes noticeable symptoms or functional impairment and may require active treatment or monitoring.
Example source variable description: BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 2=MODERATE|F136 TTE LVH: Moderate

description: BDC-HM meaning: a condition that causes significant symptoms or functional impairment, often requiring urgent or intensive intervention.
Example source variable description: BODY EXAMINATION: DEGREE OF OBESITY: 3=MARKED|F136 TTE LVH: Severe

description: (Required.) Use this slot to record the status of the Condition instance at the time of the report. If the participant was asked if they have a condition, this slot is analogous to their Yes/No/I don't know answer. Sometimes several variables are needed. Decision table: (1) Ever had X = yes and still have X = yes: PRESENT. (2) Ever = yes and still = no: HISTORICAL. (3) Ever = yes and no still-have item: PRESENT for chronic or permanent conditions (diabetes, hypertension, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, COPD, emphysema, peripheral arterial disease) because the condition or its sequelae persist; HISTORICAL for self-limited or episodic events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, TIA, pneumonia, empyema, COVID-19, pertussis, acute bronchitis) unless the variable itself says current; a variable worded history of, prior or past is HISTORICAL either way (judgment call: Anne to confirm the chronic/episodic split). (4) Ever = no: ABSENT. (5) Current item only: yes is PRESENT, no is ABSENT; a current no says nothing about earlier history. (6) Don't know, refused or missing: UNKNOWN. (7) Possible, probable, questionable or unverified wording (for example POSSIBLE CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE, Questionable CVA): UNKNOWN, a lossy mapping, never PRESENT. (8) Time-window items (last 6 months, within 1 year, since last contact): PRESENT means the Condition occurred in that window; a no is ABSENT only for that window and does not exclude earlier occurrence; record the window through the visit or age_at_condition_report. Condition ever-had, DrugExposure ever-taken and Procedure ever-done follow different rules on purpose: a stopped drug (exposure_status HISTORICAL) or a resolved episodic event is no longer present, a chronic condition persists, and a done procedure stays done (procedure_status PRESENT).
Example source variable description: Asthma: Have you ever had asthma|Asthma: Do you still have asthma|TIA last 6 months|F136 History of CHD within 1 year|Definite/Probable Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH)|FDI: OTHER HEART DISEASE (CURRENT DIAGNOSIS ONLY): 2=POSSIBLE CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE|Stroke type: Questionable CVA at exam 1

description: BDC-HM meaning: the Condition was present in the Participant at observation time. Use PRESENT when the Participant has the Condition at the time of the report (a yes to a current or still-have item, or a positive derived flag at that exam). For a chronic condition an ever-had yes with no still-have item is also PRESENT (decision table item 3).
Example source variable description: The values can vary from present, yes, 1, and much more to indicate the presence of a Condition.

description: BDC-HM meaning: the Condition was absent in the Participant at observation time. Use ABSENT when the Participant does not have the Condition at the time of the report; an ever-had item answered no means never had it, which is also ABSENT. A current-only no leaves earlier history unknown to the harmonized record.
Example source variable description: The values can vary from absent, no, 0, and much more to indicate the absence of a Condition.

description: Use HISTORICAL when the Participant had the Condition before the time of the report but no longer has it (ever = yes and still-have = no), or the variable is worded as a history of or past Condition with no current status. Ever and still-have are usually two separate variables that should be combined into a single Condition instance. An ever-had yes for a self-limited or episodic event (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, TIA, pneumonia) with no current item is also HISTORICAL; see the decision table.
Example source variable description: The values can indicate the previous presence of a condition, but often Participants are asked if they have ever had a Condition and then are asked if they still have a Condition. These data are in two separate variables that should be combined in a single Condition instance.

description: Use UNKNOWN when the Participant reports they don't know, refuses, or the answer is missing, and for possible, probable or questionable wording where the Condition is not confirmed.
Example source variable description: The values can vary from unknown, don't know, refuse to answer, and much more to indicate that the Condition status is unknown.

description: (Required.) Use this slot to record who the Condition instance is attributed to: the participant or a relative. Sometimes a Participant is asked about their family medical history and this is how that is recorded in BDC-HM. Attribution rule: the Condition, its condition_status and its ages belong to the relative named, so a No about the mother is ABSENT for the mother, not for the Participant. Combined wording that names several relatives (for example parents) uses the combined value (NATURAL_PARENT, NATURAL_SIBLING, BLOOD_RELATIVE) rather than guessing one. This information is usually contained in the source variable description.
This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant. This is the most commonly used value for this slot. This should be the default.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant's mother. The age of the Participant's mother might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Did your natural mother ever have any of the following diseases? Stroke? Q15d [Home Interview. HOM. Visit 1]|Q20a. Did your mother have [or does she have] stroke? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant's father. The age of the Participant's father might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Did your natural father ever have any of the following diseases? Stroke? Q23d [Home Interview. HOM. Visit 1]

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to the Participant's natural parent when the source says parent, or either parent, without naming mother or father. The age of the parent might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's children. The age of the child might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Q41a. Have kids been told they had stroke? [Visit 1] [Personal and Family Health History Form, PFH]|FAMILY HISTORY OF STROKE: CHILDREN

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's blood relatives, but does not specify which. Use it only when no more specific relationship is named (not for mother, father, parent, sibling or child). The age of the relative might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
Example source variable description: Family History of heart attack|Have any of your first degree blood relatives (parent, sibling, child) had pulmonary hypertension

description: This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's brothers. The age of the Participant's brother might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's sisters. The age of the Participant's sister might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.

This value specifies that the Condition instance applies to one or more of the Participant's siblings, but does not specify brother or sister. The age of the Participant's sibling might be provided in another variable and this should be included in age at condition start.
